section.title: Introduction and Overview
section.p: OS_Memory calls have been updated. The following lists the reason codes which are allocated :

value-table.value: Reserved for internal use. See PRM 5a-64
Read size of physical memory arrangement table. See PRM 5a-65 and this document
Read physical memory arrangement table. See PRM 5a-66 and this document
Read memory amounts. See PRM 5a-68 and this document
Read controller presence and logical base address. See PRM 5a-69 and this document
Lock free pool. See this document
Map PCI memory. See this document
Check memory access. See this document
Read controller presence and physical base address. See this document

swi-definition.name: OS_Memory
swi-definition.description: Read size of physical memory arrangement table

entry.register-use: 6 (reason code), all flag bits are currently reserved and must be 0
7 (reason code), all flag bits are currently reserved and must be 0
Pointer to table to fill in

use.p: This SWI is now deprecated and may not return reliable information for a given OS version.

entry.register-use:
8 + flags:
Type of memory:
DRAM VRAM ROM I/O Softload ROM Reserved
Reserved, must be 0

use.p: This SWI is used to read the amount of various types of memory available within the machine. On modern versions of RISC OS, the amount of VRAM will be returned as 0, as VRAM is now reserved to the video driver, rather than the Kernel. The new type 5 for softload RAM indicates the amount of memory allocated from DRAM (and excluded from the value returned for type 1).

swi-definition.name: OS_Memory
swi-definition.description: Read controller presence and base logical address

entry.register-use: 9 (reason code), all flag bits are currently reserved and must be 0

Controller ID:
Controller sequence number Controller type:
EASI card access speed control EASI space VIDC1 VIDC20 Reserved

use.p: This SWI is used to read the base address of a controller in logical address space. Under modern versions of the OS the correct way to obtain access to a controller is to create a dynamic area with the controller address mapped in to it. The Kernel will not map parts of hardware memory in future versions. This SWI is thus less useful in modern OS versions. Its behaviour has been changed slightly to correct an oversight in the original design. The original definition stated that 0 could be returned for an absent controller, in addition to an error being reported for an invalid controller. The implementation now returns an error for all controllers which do not exist, and 0 will not be returned.
See PRM 5a-69 for the original definition.

entry.register-use:
10 + flags:
Call made by Wimp Reserved, must be 0

use.p: This SWI was allocated in RISC OS 4 for locking the free pool in order to implement Wimp_ClaimFreeMemory. The Wimp_ClaimFreeMemory call should not be used and this call is no longer used.

entry.register-use:
11 + flags:
Set to read information, clear to map PCI space Reserved, must be 0

use.p: This SWI was allocated in RISC OS 4 for mapping PCI memory within the Phoebe hardware. PCI memory allocation should now be performed by clients through the PCI manager module. The PCI manager module will use physical memory areas to provide drivers with memory mappings. This call is no longer used.

entry.register-use:
12 + flags:
Set if pages should be in DMA-able memory Reserved, must be 0
Size of contiguous region of physical memory required in bytes
Log base 2 of required alignment of base of region within physical memory, between 12 (4K) and 30 (2G)

exit.register-use: Page number of first page which fulfills the requirements specified

use.p: This SWI is used to recommend pages of physical RAM which are unallocated and may be used for a new dynamic area. It is expected that they will be used to create a dynamic area, or to extend an existing area. An error will be returned if no pages match the required criteria. Prior to Kernel 8.77, bit 8 was not supported. This SWI call is available from RISC OS 4 onward.

entry.register-use: 24 (reason code), all flag bits are currently reserved and must be 0

exit.register-use:
Access flags:
Range is completely readable in user mode Range is completely writable in user mode Range is completely readable in privileged modes Range is completely writable in privileged modes Range is partially readable in user mode Range is partially writable in user mode Range is partially readable in privileged modes Range is partially writable in privileged modes Range is completely physically mapped Range is completely abortable (aborts handled by code) Reserved for future expansion Range is partially physically mapped Range is partially abortable (aborts handled by code) Reserved for future expansion Reserved for future expansion

use.p: This SWI is used to determine the accessibility of a range of memory. It is similar to the call in that it uses the Dynamic Area details to determine the availability of memory areas. The region from 'low address' to 'high address'-1 will be considered.

The flags returned indicate the access which is available for the range. Because the range may span (multiple) page boundaries the access for the range may vary across its length. Consequently, the two extents of accessibility are returned. Bits are separated into pairs of 4 bits. The lower 4 bits indicate the lowest level of accessibility for the region specified. The upper 4 bits indicate the highest level of accessibility for the region specified. If the bit sets are identical then the accessibility of the region does not change.

swi-definition.name: OS_Memory
swi-definition.description: Read controller presence and base physical address

entry.register-use: 25 (reason code), all flag bits are currently reserved and must be 0

Controller ID:
Controller sequence number Controller type:
EASI card access speed control EASI space VIDC1 VIDC20 Reserved for Pace OS variants Expansion ROMs Reserved for Pace OS variants Primary ROM IOMD FDC37C665 or similar Reserved for future hardware

use.p: This call checks for the presence of a given controller and returns its physical address. This allows hardware drivers to provide support for specific controllers which may exist at different physical locations on other hardware. This call is similar to OS_Memory 9.

revision.change: Corrected the description of the result of OS_Memory 9, which gave it as the controller physical address although the call reads the logical address, 'Read size of physical memory arrangement tabl', 'been been changed' and 'which are may exist'. The reason code names (such as OS_Memory_CheckAccess) are descriptive labels for the reason codes and not names defined by the operating system.
